data.name: CarIntro
data.value: Everything below the form is what the controller is running with, read from the configuration at startup. The form changes what the next start reads: restart to apply it, then check the account below.

data.name: PortalIntro
data.value: Asks {0} for {1} once, when you press the button. {2} runs on no schedule and its result goes nowhere else — not to the dashboard card, not to any charging decision. Use it to check that the credentials work and that the portal's fields are understood, whether or not the scheduled feed is on.

data.name: PortalFieldsHint
data.value: Those are the {0}, {1}, {2} and {3} fields in the form above; fill them in and restart. The portal also delivers nothing until you enable a {4} by hand — see {5}.

data.name: SignsInAfresh
data.value: Each press signs in again. That is fine by hand, and it is why this is not polled: repeated sign-ins at a real identity provider can get the account locked.

data.name: FeedIntro
data.value: Asks {0} for {1} once, now — the same call the feed makes on its own schedule, just made on request. Unlike a Data Act check, the result {2} reach the dashboard card: pressing the button updates the whole UI, not only this page. The feed's own schedule is not affected.

data.name: FeedAskHint
data.value: If the account above is not signed in, this will show it: the feed answers with what is stopping it instead of a reading.

data.name: NothingToAskYet
data.value: Nothing to ask yet: this feed is switched on but did not start, so the controller has no client for it. Fill in the fields it needs in the form above and restart.

data.name: NothingToAskChargeOnly
data.value: Nothing to ask, because nothing reads this car — and nothing needs to. The charger, not the car, reports whether a cable is plugged in, so the dashboard shows that anyway. Without a feed, only the car's state of charge is missing, so targets are set in kWh.

data.name: WorthRetrying
data.value: Try again — this error is expected and usually clears by itself.

data.name: NotWorthRetrying
data.value: Trying again will not help. Something needs to change, or needs fixing in a browser.

data.name: NothingOnTheCard
data.value: Nothing has reached the dashboard card yet, so there is nothing to compare with. That is normal for an installation with no feed switched on: this check is the only reading.

data.name: FreshFrom
data.value: Fresh reading from {0}; the dashboard card now shows it too.

data.name: AlreadyHeld
data.value: The feed already had this reading; it is not new.

data.name: NothingDescribed
data.value: No car is described yet, so every charging limit comes from the installation and targets cannot be set as a state of charge. That is a supported setup — charging still works — and the form above changes it.

data.name: NarrowerOfTwo
data.value: The controller uses the narrower of the two ranges. A car can only {0} a limit — the installation's maximum is set by the supply and the wiring, not by preference — and anything the car does not state uses the installation's value.

data.name: NoManufacturerFeed
data.value: No manufacturer feed is running. Charging is unaffected; what is missing is the car's own state of charge, so a target is asked for in kWh rather than as a percentage.

data.name: CarBatteryPressHint
data.value: The car's own state of charge, as returned for this check. Not the home battery.

data.name: CarRangeHint
data.value: The car's own estimate of its remaining range, based on its recent consumption. Nothing here plans with it; it helps you judge whether the charge you are about to request is enough.

data.name: CarReadingAgeHint
data.value: How long ago the car itself produced this reading — not when you pressed the button. A few hours is normal for a parked car.

data.name: CarChargeStateHint
data.value: What the car reports it is doing: Idle, Charging, Complete, or Unknown when it does not report.

data.name: CarPlugStateHint
data.value: Whether the car reports a cable in its socket. This is separate from the charger's status and updates much more slowly.

data.name: TargetSocHint
data.value: The charge limit set in the car or its app. Only the Data Act portal provides it; no plan uses it yet (#101). A dash means this source did not provide it.

data.name: TimeLeftHint
data.value: The car's own estimate of how much longer it needs to charge, not ours. A dash means the source did not provide it — which is useful to know.

data.name: CaptureTimeNote
data.value: The capture time is when the {0} took the reading, not now. A parked car that last reported hours ago is normal, not a fault — its state of charge does not change.

data.name: OwnTopicNothingToPress
data.value: Nothing to press, because nothing here fetches: you publish this car's readings yourself to {0} — one JSON object per reading, with the time the {1} took it in {2}, and {3}, {4}, {5} and {6} where your source has them.
data.comment: {0} is the topic (or TheTopicInTheForm), {1} is OwnTopicNothingToPress_Cars in italics, {2}–{6} are JSON field names.

data.name: TheTopicInTheForm
data.value: the topic in the form above

data.name: LastArrived
data.value: The last message carried {0}, captured {1} ago.

data.name: CardShowing
data.value: The dashboard card shows {0} from {1}, captured {2} ago{3}. That is a separate reading taken at a different time, so a difference alone is not a fault.
data.comment: {3} is SameSoc or PointsBelow/PointsAbove, with its leading space, or nothing.

data.name: OwnTopicToo
data.value: This car also has its own topic, {0}. It can run alongside a manufacturer feed; the newest reading wins.

data.name: CarReadOnly
data.value: Read-only, because this UI has no login. These fields include a manufacturer account's password, and without a login anyone on the LAN could read the car or change which account it is read from. Configure {0} ({1}) to edit them here; until then, change them in {2} and restart.

data.name: CarSaveNote
data.value: A save is checked the same way startup checks the configuration, and only values that differ are written to {0}. That file overrides {1} key by key, so each field shows where its value comes from. Nothing changes until the controller restarts — and saving cannot prove an account, because the feed is built from these keys at startup. Restart, then {2} and ask the car.

data.name: SignInIdChanged
data.value: The brand's sign-in id has changed

data.name: SignInIdChangedNote
data.value: The portal's client ids are reverse-engineered, not published, so one can stop working without warning. The symptom is a sign-in that fails as if the password were wrong. An id entered here overrides the brand above.

data.name: CarFieldsNote
data.value: These fields make charging correct, and they do not depend on any feed. The installation allows {0}–{1} A; the controller uses the narrower of the two ranges, and a car can only lower a limit.

data.name: NotSaved
data.value: Not saved — the controller would refuse to start with this:

data.name: HintUsablePack
data.value: usable, not the brochure's gross figure

data.name: HintMinCurrent
data.value: the lowest current the car will start charging at

data.name: SavedRestartSignIn
data.value: Saved. Restart the controller to apply it, then sign in.

data.name: SavedRunning
data.value: Saved. The controller is already running with these values.

data.name: KeptInSecretStore
data.value: Kept in the secret store — {0}. Leave it empty to keep it unchanged; Remove deletes it.

data.name: FeedDataAct
data.value: Audi · SEAT · Cupra · Bentley · VW commercial

data.name: FreshVolkswagen
data.value: about 20 s, plug state, live while charging

data.name: NoteVolkswagen
data.value: volkswagen.de, read live. The first sign-in always needs a one-time code e-mailed to this account, so it is done under Account below, after the restart.

data.name: NoteSkoda
data.value: The MyŠkoda Public API. It needs no password: create an API key in the MyŠkoda app and paste it under Account below. Keys expire, so they are renewed there, not here.

data.name: NoteDataAct
data.value: The EU Data Act portal — for a Group brand with no live feed of its own. It delivers data in batches, so expect the car's state of charge to be hours old, and no plug state at all.

data.name: NoteOwnTopic
data.value: An MQTT topic you publish to yourself. The broker and its credentials are the house broker's and are set in the Vehicle section; only the topic belongs to the car.

data.name: NoteNone
data.value: No feed. This is a supported setup, not an unfinished form: every EV with a Type 2 inlet charges without one. The only difference is that targets are set in kWh rather than as a state of charge, because nothing reports how much the battery already holds.

data.name: TitleWebUi
data.value: Saved from this page in {0}; overrides .env.

data.name: TitleEnvironment
data.value: {0}, from .env under Docker or /etc/gleanvolt/gleanvolt.env under systemd.

data.name: TitleCommandLine
data.value: A command-line argument, which wins over this page.

data.name: TitleDefault
data.value: Set nowhere; the built-in default applies.

data.name: Empty
data.comment: A field the car reported with no value.

data.name: AccountDataAct
data.value: This portal signs in on every read, so there is no session to set up here. The account is the VW ID and password in the form above; asking the car below checks them.

data.name: AccountOwnTopic
data.value: Nothing signs in here: you publish the readings yourself, so no manufacturer account is involved. The broker's credentials are the house broker's and are set in the Vehicle section.

data.name: AccountChargeOnly
data.value: No account, because nothing reads this car. Charging is unaffected — a target is asked for in kWh rather than as a state of charge.

data.name: NoAccountYet
data.value: There is no account to sign in to yet.

data.name: DiagnosticsIntro_0
data.value: why is that field a dash

data.name: DiagnosticsIntro
data.value: What the portal delivered and how much of it this build understands. This answers {0} — open it when a figure above is missing; otherwise you can ignore it.

data.name: FieldMoments
data.value: Each with the time the {0} reported it. A read merges several deliveries, so two figures here can be hours apart — without the times, a coarse reading and a stale one are easy to confuse.

data.name: NothingInVocabulary
data.value: None of the fields in the bundle is in the vocabulary, so these are names to add, not a car reporting empty values.

data.name: NeverBecameReading
data.value: What the bundle held that was not turned into a reading

data.name: UnmappedNote
data.value: If a value above is missing, its real name is probably in this list. The portal's vocabulary was written from VW's data dictionary, not from your car, so this is expected on a first run and is not a fault. The fix is to add the right names to {0}; pasting this list into an issue is enough for someone else to do it.

data.name: AllRecognised
data.value: Every field in the bundle was recognised.

data.name: OdometerNote
data.value: The odometer is delivered, but nothing uses it. Target SOC would let a plan reject an impossible battery target; that is deferred in {0}.

data.name: PhasesNotStated
data.value: Not stated — the installation's count is used

data.name: NoAccountExplanation
data.value: No manufacturer account is set up, so there is nothing to sign in to. A feed that needs one offers its own sign-in once all its required fields are filled in and the controller has restarted.
